seoTitle: Cheapest Heater to Run UK: Costs per Hour 2026
title: Cheapest electric heater to run UK: real costs per hour and the best buys
description: Which electric heater is cheapest to run in the UK? Hourly costs at today's price cap, plus fan, convector, oil-filled and halogen heaters checked today.
intro:
**The cheapest electric heater to run is the one with the lowest wattage that still warms your room, with a thermostat to switch it off once it's warm. Every plug-in heater turns electricity into heat at about the same efficiency, so a £6 fan heater and a £400 Dyson cost the same per kWh.** At the current price cap rate of 26.32p per kWh, a 2kW heater on full power costs about 53p an hour, a 1.5kW model about 39p and a 1.2kW halogen about 32p.

For most people, the best-value buy right now is a thermostat convector such as the Bush 2kW at £21 at Argos, or an oil-filled radiator if you want steady heat for hours. Prices checked on retailers' own pages on 13 November 2026.

deals.name: Bush 2kW Convector Heater (DF2362)
deals.note: Three power levels (750W, 1,250W and 2kW) and an adjustable thermostat, so you can run it at the low setting and let it cycle. The best low-cost pick for heating one room evenly.

deals.name: Challenge NT20-20A 2kW Ceramic Fan Heater
deals.note: A third off an already cheap heater, with a thermostat and three settings. Fan heaters warm you quickly, so they're cheapest for short bursts in a small room or under a desk.

deals.name: Igenix 2000W Convector Heater
deals.note: A simple three-setting convector with an adjustable thermostat. Slightly dearer than the Bush model above, but a sound choice if you're already shopping at Dunelm.

deals.name: Pro Breeze 2000W Mini Ceramic Fan Heater
deals.note: A compact fan heater with three heat modes, a fan-only setting and a thermostat. Cheaper on Pro Breeze's own site than the £31.99 PriceSpy shows at Amazon.

deals.name: Dreo Atom Core 1.5kW Ceramic Space Heater
deals.note: Tops out at 1.5kW and has an eco mode that varies power between 900W and 1,500W, which keeps costs down in a small room. Full price at the moment, so wait for Black Friday if you can.

deals.name: De'Longhi Dragon 4 2.5kW Oil Filled Radiator
deals.note: Argos's product page showed £152 when we checked (its category page still said £190, so confirm in your basket). Oil-filled radiators hold heat after the thermostat cuts out, which suits long evenings in a bigger room.

deals.name: Beldray 1.2kW Halogen Heater
deals.note: The lowest-wattage heater here, at about 32p an hour on full. Halogens warm the person in front of them rather than the room, so they're best in draughty spaces or a garden room.

deals.name: Dyson Purifier Hot+Cool Gen1 (HP10)
deals.note: £150 off Dyson's own price. It won't cost less to run than a £21 heater, but it also purifies the air and works as a fan in summer, which is where the money goes.

body:
## Which type of electric heater is cheapest to run?

Here's the part most adverts skip: all plug-in electric heaters are close to 100% efficient. Every kWh you pay for comes out as heat, whether it's a fan heater, a convector, an oil-filled radiator or a halogen. Which? makes the same point: heaters are very efficient at turning electricity into heat whatever they cost. So no type is magically cheaper per unit of heat.

What changes the bill is:

- **Wattage.** A 2kW heater on full uses 2kWh an hour. A 1.2kW one uses 1.2kWh.
- **A thermostat or eco mode.** This is the biggest saving. Once the room hits your set temperature, the heater switches off or turns down. Without one, it runs flat out until you remember to turn it off.
- **How long it runs and how big the space is.** Heating one small room for two hours is cheap. Heating a draughty open-plan room all evening isn't.
- **How the heat is delivered.** This decides which type suits you, as below.

## Which type suits which room?

- **Fan heaters** (ceramic or standard) warm the air fast and are cheapest for short bursts: a bathroom before a shower, a home office for an hour, a cold bedroom at night. They're noisy and lose heat as soon as they stop.
- **Convector heaters** warm the whole room more evenly and quietly. With a thermostat, they're the best all-rounder for a bedroom or spare room for a few hours.
- **Oil-filled radiators** take 20 minutes or so to warm up, but the oil keeps radiating heat after the thermostat cuts out, so they cycle less. They're the best choice for long evenings, and they're silent.
- **Halogen and infrared heaters** heat the person rather than the air. At 1.2kW or less they're cheap to run, and good for draughty spaces where warm air escapes, but they won't warm a room.

## What does an electric heater cost to run?

At the Ofgem price cap of 26.32p per kWh (1 October to 31 December 2026; electricity carries no VAT until 31 March 2027, so that's the rate you pay):

- **1.2kW halogen:** about 32p an hour.
- **1.5kW eco fan heater:** about 39p an hour on full.
- **2kW fan or convector heater:** about 53p an hour on full.
- **2.5kW oil-filled radiator:** about 66p an hour on full.

With a thermostat cycling it on and off, real costs fall well below these figures once the room is warm. Running a 2kW convector for four hours an evening at an average of 1kW costs about £1.05 a night, or roughly £7.40 a week.

The cap for January to March 2027 is due on 25 November. Forecasters expect electricity to rise to around 30p per kWh, which would add about 7p an hour to a 2kW heater on full.

## Is an electric heater cheaper than central heating?

Usually not for the whole house. Gas is 7.97p per kWh under the current cap, about a third of the price of electricity, so gas central heating is cheaper per unit of heat. A plug-in heater only saves money when you heat one room you're sitting in and turn the central heating down elsewhere. The Energy Saving Trust also notes that heat pumps are around three times more efficient than standard electric heaters, and storage heaters on an off-peak tariff are cheaper to run than direct electric heating.

If you mainly want to keep yourself warm, an [electric blanket](/guides/electric-blanket-deals-uk/) costs a few pence an hour, far less than any heater. A [dehumidifier](/guides/dehumidifier-deals-uk/) also helps, because dry air heats up more easily.

## What's a good price?

- **Basic 2kW fan heater:** under £15. The Challenge at £6.40 is about as low as it gets.
- **2kW convector with a thermostat:** £20 to £30.
- **2kW to 2.5kW oil-filled radiator:** £40 to £60 for a budget model, around £150 for a De'Longhi Dragon.
- **Dyson Hot+Cool:** under £400. Dyson's AM09 is £399.99 on its own site, which is its normal price, not a deal.

## Buy now or wait for Black Friday?

Budget heaters rarely get cheaper than they are now, so if you're cold, buy one. Pricier models such as the Dreo, the De'Longhi Dragon range and Dyson's heaters are worth waiting for until 27 November. See [every Black Friday 2026 guide](/black-friday/) for other home deals, and our [heated clothes airer guide](/guides/heated-clothes-airer-deals-uk/) for another cheap winter buy.

## Electric heater FAQs

### What is the cheapest electric heater to run per hour?

The one with the lowest wattage that still keeps you warm. A 1.2kW halogen costs about 32p an hour on full at today's price cap, against about 53p for a 2kW heater. A thermostat matters more than the type.

### Are oil-filled radiators cheaper to run than fan heaters?

Not per kWh: both turn electricity into heat at the same efficiency. Oil-filled radiators hold heat and cycle less once a room is warm, so they can work out cheaper over a long evening. Fan heaters are cheaper for short bursts.

### Do eco or low-energy heaters really save money?

Only by using fewer watts or switching off sooner. An eco mode that drops from 1.5kW to 900W saves money, but you get less heat. Watch out for adverts claiming a heater uses less electricity to make the same heat; that isn't possible.

### Is it safe to leave an electric heater on overnight?

It's best not to. If you do use one in a bedroom, choose a model with a thermostat, tip-over switch and overheat protection, keep it a metre from bedding and curtains, and plug it straight into the wall rather than an extension lead.

### Is it cheaper to heat one room with an electric heater than to put the central heating on?

It can be, if you turn the central heating down and only heat the room you're in for a few hours. For the whole house, gas central heating is cheaper.
